title: The Day of the Kettle Conspiracy
skyStory: Ten percent of the moon is showing, which is the lunar equivalent of peeking through the blinds. Sagittarius is packing its bags for tomorrow's move and keeps finding things it forgot it owned: a compass, three arrows, a half-written postcard to Saturn. The kettle in every kitchen is in on this somehow. Nobody will say how.

reading: Your brain will hand you eleven brilliant ideas before breakfast. The Tiger loves a buffet. But a very serious knight is standing in the doorway with its arms crossed, and it only lets one idea through. Pick the one that makes you laugh, not the one that makes you busy.

Somewhere around 1:05 pm a kettle, a microwave or a dryer will beep at you three times. Each beep is a question. First: is this the main thing? Second: have you looked out a window today? Third: have you told anyone that they did a good job? Answer all three before the next beep, or the appliances win.
joel.mission: Make a list of ten ideas, then cross out nine with great ceremony, saying 'not today, friend' to each one.
joel.omen: Steam fogging a window in the shape of a lopsided heart. Someone is thinking about you warmly.
joel.elementWhy: aim it, do not spray it

reading: The shore is quiet today and so are you, in the good way, the way a cat is quiet right before it does something magnificent. People will expect you to talk first. Let the silence stretch one extra beat. Somebody will rush to fill it and reveal exactly what you needed to know.

The [[Six of Swords]] has its little boat out today, and the water is calm for once. Whatever you have been carrying across, set one small piece of it down in the hull and let the boat do some of the work. You do not have to row and steer and carry all at once. Joel is on the far bank, waving his arms too much.
nancy.mission: Leave the room one minute early from something today and spend that minute looking at the horizon or the nearest tree.
nancy.omen: A boat, a canoe or even a picture of one. The crossing is going better than you think.
nancy.stoneWhy: layer by layer, like the tide
nancy.elementWhy: a light breeze in the sails

together.text: Pick one thing each that you will absolutely finish by Friday. Say it to the other person in one sentence, no hedging allowed. Then check in Friday night with a single word: done, nearly or sneakily rebranded. All three are acceptable answers, but only one gets a cheer.
